findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 There wasn't any paper towels available at the hand-sink in the back storage area. Discussed with PIC and paper towels were provided. PIC mentioned that paper towels dispenser was broken. Ensure that the necessary repairs is done on the paper towel dispenser in the area mentioned. Be sure that paper towels are available at every hand-sink  to ensure hands are getting washed properly.  

Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 There was no sani bucket available at the beginning of the inspection. PIC was made aware of the sani bucket being empty and a new sani bucket was made.  Ensure that there is sanitizer in the sani bucket at all times to ensure proper sanitary cleaning of food-contact surfaces.

(E) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (E) If a chemical SANITIZER other than chlorine, iodine, or a quaternary ammonium compound is used, it shall be applied in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: An insect glue trap was stored in close proximity of clean dishes in the dish room. Discussed and showed to PIC. Ensure that glue traps are never stored near clean dishes to avoid contaminating food.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: The prep table in the back of the house is stored underneath vent covers that are significantly covered in dust. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that vent covers are frequently cleaned to prevent buildup and contaminating food items during preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in disrepair:
- cabinet doors are missing from the cabinet space across from the serving freezers (in front of house) - cabinets store single service items
- the leg of the prep table in the back of the house is broken and is wrapped in duck tape - causing the table to be unleveled

Ensure that pieces of equipment are repaired.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.11(A) Good Repair and Proper Adjustment. (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following nonfood contact surfaces were observed soiled:
- there was a buildup of mold along the back of the triple sink in the BOH - clean mold and re-caulk sink to wall
- several nonfood contact surfaces such as counter tops, inside of cabinets, sides of equipment, etc. were observed with a buildup up food residue and other debris

Ensure that these area are cleaned/sanitized frequently to prevent buildup and the presence of mold.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: There was a leak coming from the faucet of the triple sink. Discussed and shown to PIC. Ensure that the triple sink’s faucet is repaired and is in leak free condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following areas are in need of repair and cleaning:
- there are missing ceiling tiles above single service items in the storage room
- overall, floors, walls, and ceilings throughout the front and back of house are in need of a deep cleaning. Splatter and debris are observed on surfaces. 
Ensure that physical facilities are maintained and cleaned as frequent as necessary.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed wet mop head stored in basin of mop sink. Discussed with PIC and mop head was turned upside down. Ensure that wet mop heads are stored in a manner that allows for them to properly air dry.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:

2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:

5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
The employees working at the time of the inspection were not food handler certified. Ensure that all employees are food handler certified if they handle food. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

Observed no certified food protection manager (CFPM) for the facility. Facility PIC stated she is a food handler. Ensure facility has a CFPM during all operational hours. Ensure facility has at least 2 CFPM’s to cover all hours. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

(REPEAT) Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements for the facility. PIC was unsure if the facility has them. Provided copy for the facility. Ensure all staff reads and signs. Keep in a public health folder/binder. Ensure new hires read and sign the document. Inspector will follow-up on 12/26/23. Repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 11/3/22.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no Norovirus illness clean-up policy for the facility. Facility was provided a copy of the policy SCDPH uses. Ensure the facility has bleach to perform the procedure. Facility may also purchase a bodily fluid clean-up kit that kills for Norovirus. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed the employee to wash hands then turn the faucet handles off without a barrier. Discussed with employee. Ensure proper hand washing with hot water, soap, and paper towels. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is used to turn off faucet handles. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed the milk in the bottom reach-in cooler to be dated from 12/5/23. Observed the almond milk in the same cooler to be dated 10/18/23. Employee discarded both cartons. Ensure a 7-day date marking system is observed. Ensure items are discarded within the 7-day date mark. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

(REPEAT) Observed no thermometers in the bottom reach-in cooler and the walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC. Ensure hanging thermometers are provided for cold holding units. Ensure extra thermometers are available at the facility. Correct by next routine inspection. Repeat from last routine inspection on 11/3/22.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no copies of food handler’s licenses for the facility. Ensure all new hires obtain a food handler’s license within 30-days of employment. Ensure copies are left at the facility in a public health folder/binder. Food handler’s licenses are valid for 3 years. Correct by next routine inspection.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Milk in the prep cooler was not date marked. The manager stated milk is not used within 24 hours after opening. All TCS foods must be date marked with a 7 day date marking if held for more than 24 hours. The milk was date marked during the inspection. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C).

findings.comment:
There was not a thermometer observed in the walk in cooler. Ensure a thermometer is provided to ensure the air temperature can be measured inside the walk in cooler.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
A wet wiping cloth was observed on the counter. Ensure wet wiping cloths are held in sanitizer solutions. See below for wiping cloth requirements. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.comment:
REPEAT> Drain pipes under dipper wells still extend into slightly into the floor drain. Make sure that drain pipes have at least a 1" air gap between the top of the floor drain.
750-1080 The potable water system shall be installed to preclude the possibility of backflow.  Devices to protect against backflow and back siphonage shall be installed at all fixtures and equipment where an air gap at least twice the diameter of the water inlet is not provided between the water outlet from the fixture and the fixture’s flood-level rim and wherever else backflow or backsiphonage may occur. Install backflow prevention device.

750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
